note: Triennial election of Down County Council, polled Thursday 5 June 1958. There was no contest: 'There will be no contest for Down County Council. Eighteen of the 20 former members of the Council were nominated yesterday and the two new nominees were also unopposed' (Belfast News-Letter, 21 May 1958, p. 7). The continuation of that report, headed 'CANDIDATES FOR COUNTY COUNCILS (Continued from page 7)', is on p. 11 of the same issue and names the member returned for every one of the twenty divisions. The two new members were Mr. John Johnston (Saintfield), who succeeded Col. Michael C. Perceval-Price, and Capt. David J. R. Ker (Donaghadee), who succeeded Mr. Alexander Adair; both retiring members had represented their divisions for many years. The paper prints addresses and occupations but no party labels, so no party is recorded. The paper prints the division as 'Rathfryland' with a '(sic)'. Addresses and occupations printed with the names are not reproduced (privacy rule; gap-fill 6 Nov 2026). Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Rathfryland' to Rathfriland (19 Nov 2026, w19-tidy, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the Northern Ireland county electoral division maps of 1930-69 name the division Rathfriland; the rounds were filed as Rathfriland (1924, 1927, 1930, 1933, 1936, 1939, 1946, 1949, 1952, 1964); Rathfryland (1955, 1958, 1961, 1967). This round was filed as 'Rathfryland', kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (rathfryland) answers with a redirect to this one.
